title: Compare one action at a time
takeaway: An observed change gives a lead. Repeating it helps test an explanation.
alt: 100 gold becomes 101 after one coin; repeat the controlled action before explaining its cause.
heading: Check whether the evidence answers your question

title: An update and a drawing are separate work
takeaway: The CPU changes stored state; drawing turns that state into a picture.
alt: RAM stores gold, a CPU instruction changes it, and drawing shows the new amount.
heading: The parts work together

title: A comparison chooses the next operation
takeaway: If gold is below the cost, this purchase branch is skipped.
alt: A purchase compares the gold with the price before subtracting the price.
heading: An algorithm is a repeatable procedure

title: A pause connects code with current state
takeaway: Inspect the instruction and its inputs before stepping it.
alt: An instruction subtracts five from gold; the before and after values show its effect.
heading: A debugger can pause and inspect a running program

title: A detour must reconnect with normal execution
takeaway: Displaced work still needs to happen exactly once.
alt: The hook sends execution to extra code, which performs displaced work and resumes at untouched code.
heading: A detour needs five parts

title: A detour borrows state from its caller
takeaway: Preserve the values that the continuation still needs.
alt: Incoming register and flag values survive the added work when the continuation depends on them.
heading: Preserve the interrupted calculation

title: Several clues are stronger than one shape
takeaway: These shapes suggest an object; symbols and repeated traces test it.
alt: A receiver, repeated field offsets, and an indirect function call together suggest object-oriented code.
heading: Source patterns do not survive as labels

title: A collection can outgrow its allocation
takeaway: Growth may move storage, so an old element address can become stale.
alt: Appending a third item to storage for two can require a new allocation and invalidate old element addresses.
heading: Recognize behavior before naming a container

title: Stored bits and their meaning can differ
takeaway: XOR with the same key again recovers 125.
alt: The value 125 XOR 90 is stored as 39; applying the same XOR key recovers the original value.
heading: Obfuscation changes the representation

title: A system sees the version it was given
takeaway: A copied snapshot can lag even while live state changes.
alt: Input requests movement, simulation updates position, and rendering consumes a chosen snapshot.
heading: A frame is a fixed list of schedules

title: A short capture separates timing from storage
takeaway: A full queue needs an explicit drop, wait, or overwrite choice.
alt: The game thread captures a small event into a bounded queue and a writer formats and saves it later.
heading: The recorder must not stall the game

title: A visible target must pass all three checks
takeaway: A failed check explains why a nearby target may remain unseen.
alt: An NPC tests distance, view angle, and obstacles before treating a player as visible.
heading: The three checks in code

title: A public name leads through an index
takeaway: An exported name can lead to another DLL rather than local code.
alt: The export name maps to an ordinal index, then to an address-table entry containing an RVA or a forwarder.
heading: An export table is a DLL's public index

title: Instruction lengths decide the next start
takeaway: Starting inside an instruction can produce a plausible wrong decoding.
alt: A three-byte instruction followed by a two-byte instruction puts the next boundary at byte offset five.
heading: Decoding is harder than formatting

title: A relative call uses the next address
takeaway: The return address is 0x1005; the displacement is signed.
alt: A five-byte call at hexadecimal 1000 adds displacement 20 to next address 1005 to reach target 1025.
heading: What a `call` instruction really does

title: Restoration needs the bytes that were replaced
takeaway: Do not release cave storage while execution can still reach it.
alt: A reversible patch records verified original bytes, installs temporary bytes, and restores the original after execution drains.
heading: Represent a patch as data

title: A held key is different from a fresh press
nodes:
Fresh press
now AND NOT old
takeaway: Pressed after pressed means held, without a new rising edge.
alt: Comparing previous and current key state distinguishes a fresh press from a held key.
heading: State, events, and messages are not interchangeable

title: Shutdown follows the dependencies backwards
nodes:
Wait for workers
no active calls
takeaway: A component must outlive every worker still using it.
alt: Shutdown stops admission, waits for users of a component, then restores state and releases it.
heading: Combining code exposes hidden problems

title: An observing wrapper preserves the draw
takeaway: Logging changes the observation; forwarding preserves the call.
alt: A wrapper records an index count of nine and forwards the same arguments to the real OpenGL function.
heading: A wrapper records and forwards draw calls

title: Draw arguments are only part of the request
takeaway: The same count with different bound state can draw a different thing.
alt: Bound buffers and shaders combine with DrawIndexed arguments to determine the GPU work.
heading: Read the arguments precisely

title: Text uses an existing rendering context
takeaway: A correct address still needs the expected ABI and frame timing.
alt: An in-game text function combines the supplied text and position with existing font and frame state.
heading: A third option between a window and an overlay

title: Meaning comes after framing and decoding
takeaway: Reject malformed input before it reaches the command handler.
alt: A lobby client frames incoming bytes, decodes an event, and only then decides whether to reply.
heading: What we are building

title: Readers and writers need the same exclusion
takeaway: An event announces readiness; it does not itself guard a partial read.
alt: A shared mutex excludes a reader while the writer updates multiple fields; both sides take it.
heading: Processes normally have separate address spaces

title: A read can return only part of a message
takeaway: Byte-stream reads must be accumulated to the promised length.
alt: A framed named-pipe message accumulates its length and payload before parsing, even when reads return fragments.
heading: A named pipe is a local client/server channel

title: Decide the destination before writing
takeaway: Absolute paths, parent traversal, and link behavior need explicit checks.
alt: An installer checks the path and proves the final destination stays inside its mod directory before extracting bytes.
heading: An archive contains names, not trusted paths

title: Encryption and authenticity travel together
nodes:
Open with key
verify or reject
takeaway: A new nonce is required for each encryption under the same key.
alt: Authenticated encryption produces ciphertext and a tag; opening validates the tag and rejects tampering.
heading: Five tools with different jobs

title: Changing bytes need not move later fields
takeaway: These four bytes are a little-endian u32, not the text '100'.
alt: A four-byte overwrite changes a little-endian integer from 100 to 101 without inserting or deleting bytes.
heading: A binary save is not text

title: A Lua table maps keys to values
takeaway: Sequence operations add a convention: consecutive keys starting at one.
alt: A Lua table can contain integer sequence keys and named record keys; sequence operations expect a particular shape.
heading: Lua tables represent arrays, records, and maps

title: Reachability matters more than a reference cycle
takeaway: An unreachable cycle can be collected by a tracing collector.
alt: A tracing collector follows references from roots and reclaims unreachable objects, including unreachable cycles.
heading: Roots answer “what is still reachable?”

title: Call frames partition one value stack
takeaway: The VM remembers result placement and where the caller continues.
alt: Each VM call frame identifies a local range in a value stack and stores information needed to return to its caller.
heading: One value stack can hold many frames

title: A PID and a handle answer different questions
takeaway: A requested right is not permission until the OS grants it.
alt: A process ID selects the process, while a granted handle carries the operations Windows allowed.
heading: A PID identifies a process but grants no access

title: A handle does not make every page readable
takeaway: Both process access and the actual page state affect a read.
alt: Memory inspection checks process rights, page commitment and protection, and the actual returned byte count.
heading: Memory is managed in pages

title: An address is not a lifetime guarantee
takeaway: Reused storage can hold a different object at the same address.
alt: Reading a field requires a matching build layout and a still-live object, not just a plausible address.
heading: The runtime decides what an address means

title: A familiar basename is only the first clue
takeaway: Two files in different folders can share a basename.
alt: The same DLL basename can identify different files; its resolved path and build identity distinguish them.
heading: A module name is not a full identity

title: Capability detection permits a clear fallback
takeaway: Calling still requires the proven function type and ABI.
alt: An optional API is looked up in a trusted module; presence selects a correctly typed call and absence selects a fallback.
heading: Import tables are not the only way to call an API

title: Successful translation is only one check
takeaway: A valid translation can still point to the wrong object or process.
alt: Capture provenance, the address-space root, and object evidence together establish what a translated address means.
heading: A clean translation can still be the wrong one

title: Accepted state must stay inside its bounds
takeaway: The display should follow the accepted health value.
alt: Twenty damage against five health produces zero health when the simulation clamps its accepted result.
heading: An invariant is a property that must stay true

title: A passing check describes only its coverage
takeaway: Unmeasured bytes and later changes are outside this claim.
alt: An integrity result depends on the measured byte range, measurement time, and expected baseline.
heading: An integrity check is a claim about a boundary

title: A disabled button is not a command check
takeaway: The command handler must reject a disallowed transition itself.
alt: A disabled interface control does not protect a separately callable command; the command checks accepted state.
heading: What all three examples have in common

title: A virtual device is backed by host work
takeaway: Some guest instructions run directly; device handling can need an exit.
alt: A guest device request reaches a virtual device implementation that uses a host resource.
heading: What a VM exit is

title: A guest address is translated twice
takeaway: The offset within a mapped page survives each translation.
alt: Guest page tables translate guest virtual to guest physical addresses, then EPT or NPT translates to host physical memory.
heading: A worked translation

title: Each clock moves one bit through the chain
takeaway: TMS selects the TAP transition; TDI supplies the shifted data.
alt: A shift clock moves one bit into the register from TDI and one old bit out through TDO.
heading: Shift registers: many bits through one wire

title: Repeated input is an observation to explain
takeaway: Timing alone does not identify the program that produced an input.
alt: A server detector observes button edges over a window but cannot identify the originating client program from timing alone.
heading: Macrodox counts button edges

title: Each observer sees a limited part of a machine
takeaway: Permissions and observation coverage limit each conclusion.
alt: Client protection collects file, module, and process-access observations within the permissions of its execution environment.
heading: User-mode checks inspect a limited view

title: Tool location changes the available observations
takeaway: Legitimate tools can produce some of the same local signals.
alt: An external tool runs in another process and an internal tool runs inside the game, which changes the observations available to a defender.
heading: Process location changes local observations
